speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: My wife and I have four children aged between 17 and 34.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: By 2018, two of them were married and we were blessed with two grandchildren and were expecting more to come.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We decided to try to bring the entire extended family together under one roof whilst the grandchildren were still young.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think older Members will appreciate that attempting to do this requires consent and concurrence of the son-in-law, the daughter-in-law and it also means each nuclear family has to live with their children in the same bedroom.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: My children agree and we began this journey.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We were aware at that time that there were hundreds of rustic black and white bungalows scattered throughout Singapore, some of them a century old.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We had also done some initial due diligence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We went through the State Property Information Office (SPIO) website, so, we had a sense of the market at that point in time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And, of course, Members also know that if we go back to 2018, the rental market, in fact, was declining.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, in September 2018, my wife was visiting a friend and happened to drive past the property at 31 and there was a prominent "For Lease" sign with a telephone number.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: She called the number and it turned out to be a property agent from Colliers International Consultancy and Valuation Private Limited.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However, the property had been vacant for many years.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Later on, we discovered it had, in fact, been vacant since, I think, July 2013 and, unfortunately, was in an advanced state of disrepair.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Just to give Members an idea of what it looked like then: the roof was leaking; the wooden floor upstairs had holes so you could see downstairs from upstairs; the staircase, the wooden fixtures in it were rotting; there was major termite infestation and it was the first time in my life I had seen termite mounds in the garden.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And it was obvious that extensive repairs would have been necessary to make the house liveable.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Around the property itself, there were several large trees which, in fact, had uprooted, collapsed, damaged the fence, and the undergrowth was unkempt.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Actually, we saw snakes both inside and outside the house.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And there were also three adjacent properties that were undergoing comprehensive rebuilding, with all the associated noise and dust.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The managing agent from Colliers rejected this offer.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I should say they rejected the offer because they said upgrading the toilets would constitute improvement of the property.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In other words, we accepted the asking rent stipulated by the property agent and the limited scope of works proposed by the Managing Agent.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I should say, as Minister for Foreign Affairs, this is not a good example of – how shall I put it – of strenuous negotiations, because we basically gave in to what was asked in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But I should say that when I conduct foreign affairs, I am a far sharper negotiator.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I was not aware of this until CPIB published its report.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Arguably, maybe we should have held out longer.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But never mind, the point is, we signed.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, Mr Deputy Speaker, let me conclude my brief statement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: At all times, we were scrupulously careful to ensure that everything was aboveboard.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I must say the agent from Colliers and all the staff from SLA have always conducted themselves professionally and with utmost integrity in all their engagements with us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We should be grateful that we have civil servants and people from the private sector who act as our agents, who behave and conduct themselves to this standard because this maintains the integrity of our system.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I will be happy to take questions later from Members.
